shared.title: Move-In Week
shared.theme: Half house, half arena: seven days to make strangers a household, then three bouts that test it.
shared.question: Can four strangers make Sakura Lane a home in a week, and still stand together when the arena sorts them?
shared.builds_to: The placement tournament at Chikara Battle Arena (Days 6 to 7) and the night the results come home.
shared.ending_shape: bittersweet, one crack: the house holds, each housemate walks into a different class on Monday, and one moment of friction stings without becoming a wound

hidden.turning_point: Day 7 results night. PCs placed together in one specialization; housemates split (Tatsuya Strike, Mio Support, Shin Investigation, Sunny Media). Crack default: Ayame jabs Sunny ('consolation prize') within a PC's earshot in the gallery; Sunny looks at that PC before answering. Fallback, checked Day 7 morning: if no PC has had a scene with Sunny beyond her arrival, use the friction candidate (bible 4.1) for the housemate the PCs got closest to.
hidden.notes: STRUCTURE: about 60 turns in two arcs: A1 Move-In (Days 1-5, ~30), A2 Placement (Days 6-7 + results, ~30). Stakes personal: Shimazu's Day 3 warning stays background. BEATS ON THE WORLD CLOCK, not skips: Mio comes down the next time any PC is in or near the kitchen; Sunny's taxi arrives the first turn after noon wherever the PCs are (they hear the luggage); skips only per the agency rules. SPLITS: at most 3 scenes run at once (A/B/C); a 4th holds until its player acts; habit: an NPC asks two PCs along, never a director merge. HOUSE REACHES OUT: Pulse chore rota, dinner list, group chat, housemate messages; if ignored, the world moves on (dinner happens, Tatsuya saves plates). TUTORIAL: one reminder Day 4-5 if open; Tatsuya raises it Day 6 morning; then the PCs' choice stands. TOURNAMENT: every team fights all three bouts (placement, not knockout); Voyage hears this as a plain fact at the briefing (record the fact then). Bout budgets taper: R1 <=4, R2 <=6, Final <=8, one housemate gallery/bay beat between bouts; housemates' own bouts offscreen. Opponents stay as the bible has them; a PC power that hard-counters one is an earned early win, no second phase. PERSONAL MARKS: each PC gets one, drawn from their standout moment in Voyage's bout output, delivered as an ignorable offer (instructor note, elective invite) by existing staff only, never a stat. SEEDING: step-1 tells for Mio, Sunny, Shin, plus Shimazu's look at Yuto on Day 4; nothing for Arimura or Ayame. SPOTLIGHT: organic; correct when `spotlight` shows a PC at 0. Session zero: combat 3, social 3, mystery 2, exploration 1; ending hope bittersweet.

shared.title: Rice, Rotas and Strangers
shared.tone: warm and wry: banter over the stove, small frictions, something quietly off upstairs
shared.promise: Will four strangers make Sakura Lane feel like theirs before Monday starts sorting them?
shared.premise: Move-in weekend at Sakura Lane Sharehouse. The House Manager's rules are done, Tatsuya is up with rice, Shin is watching the door, Mio is only a whirr behind the loft door, and Sunny is a week late and on her way. Classes start Monday; the placement tournament is announced midweek.
shared.pressure: The house finds its rhythm on its own clock: the Pulse chore rota and dinner list go live, the welcome dinner happens with whoever comes, and orientation on Monday reminds 2B that the school expects it to fail.
set_pieces: a welcome dinner that can go either way
a house-rules standoff over quiet hours
a first power test in the training bays
shared.subplot: Sunny's late arrival strains the room count, the quiet hours and everyone's patience with her ring light.
shared.climax_kind: the tournament briefing that turns housemates into rivals for placement
shared.ending_shape: warm but unsettled: the house has a rhythm, and the first hairline crack is visible
seeds: paperclips rearranged on the sign-in sheet
a Pulse ping: the chore rota and dinner list are live
Tatsuya's tea tray, one cup rattling
wins_on_offer: Tatsuya as someone who trusts you near him
Shin starting to call the house 'ours'
the rooftop chill deck as the house's place
Yūto as an upper-year contact at the vending-machine nook
backstory_hooks: PENDING PC SHEETS: one hook per PC from their sheet (famous parent, background or gear)

twist.text: Mio's skipped meals and all-night work hide money trouble (ladder step 1 only; nothing about who she owes).

fronts.name: The House Finds Its Rhythm
fronts.goal: settle into routines with or without the PCs

moves.text: The House Manager posts the Pulse chore rota and dinner list (Day 1).
The welcome dinner happens Day 1 evening with whoever comes; Tatsuya saves plates for anyone missing.
A house group chat forms and in-jokes start (Day 2 to 3); absent PCs are tagged, not waited for.
A quiet-hours clash (Sunny's ring light, Mio's night whirr) gets settled by someone (Day 4 to 5).

fronts.name: Shimazu's Doubt
fronts.goal: show 2B the arrangement is a gamble the school expects to lose

moves.text: Orientation warning at Chikara Academy main-hall (Day 3): a verdict on a line.
A Pulse notice spreads the rumor that 2B won't last a month.
Tournament briefing (Day 4 to 5): placement carries weight; every team fights all three bouts.

fronts.name: Mio's Leak
fronts.goal: keep her trouble hidden while her power leaks

moves.text: Loft light on all night, a whirr down the hall; she misses the welcome dinner.
Paperclips and a coin drift out from under her door; she plucks them back and flees.
Her phone buzzes from an unknown number at a shared moment; she silences it: 'It's nothing, really.'

antagonist.name: Reiko Shimazu
antagonist.face: Vice Principal Reiko Shimazu: formal, conditional, distrusts the arrangement, not the students
antagonist.first_contact: Day 3 orientation at Chikara Academy/main-hall: the warning, delivered to the whole class.

clues.text: Mio pays her share of the dinner fund in counted small change, twice.
Mio says she already ate whenever food appears, and Tatsuya's face says she didn't.
A Pulse listing under Mio's handle sells a precision tool she clearly still uses.
Mio silences calls from an unknown number and goes still each time.

surprises: Paperclips rearranged into WELCOME on the sign-in sheet
Sunny's ring light flickers the whole lane's lights
Arimura leaves orientation mid-sentence and returns with snacks, saying nothing
climax_options: The briefing lands with the house together and joking about it
The briefing lands with the house scattered, each hearing it alone
Someone volunteers the house as one team and the others have to answer

shared.title: Three Bouts and a Board
shared.tone: loud, bright and nervous: arena noise, puzzle fights, a gallery that remembers everything
shared.promise: When the arena puts each of them into a class, what will the house still hold together?
shared.premise: Days 6 to 7 at Chikara Battle Arena. Every first-year team fights three bouts that decide its specialization. The four newcomers fight as one team; the housemates fight on their own teams, and the gallery is full of 1A.
shared.pressure: The placement board fills in after every bout, 1A watches from the gallery, and the results on Day 7 will send each housemate to a different class.
set_pieces: a results-night reckoning at the house
shared.subplot: Tatsuya's own bout: the strongest first-year in the building refuses to let his power go.
shared.climax_kind: the Final bout, then the results read aloud
shared.ending_shape: bittersweet, one crack: placed together, split from the housemates, one sting that does not become a wound
seeds: brackets posted at the arena entrance: three bouts for every team
an opposing captain bowing to Tatsuya in the training bays
Pulse clips of the house's bouts going around 1A
wins_on_offer: a personal mark for each PC: an instructor's eye, an elective invite or a staff contact
the crowd's memory of how the team fought
the medical station staff as allies
echoes: PENDING PLAY: fill from Move-In (Rice, Rotas and Strangers) once it closes
backstory_hooks: PENDING PC SHEETS: one hook per PC, ideally a famous parent watching or not watching from the gallery

twist.text: Sunny's brightness in the gallery is a performance: she deflects any mention of the video and there is more to it than the public version (ladder step 1 only).

fronts.name: The Placement Board
fronts.goal: sort every first-year by Day 7 evening

moves.text: Day 6 morning: brackets posted; every team fights Round 1, Round 2 and the Final.
After Round 2: provisional marks go up in the officials-booth window.
Day 7 evening: results read aloud; the housemates go to Strike, Support, Investigation and Media.
1A takes the best rows; Ayame watches without cheering.
Pulse clips of 2B's bouts circulate with mocking captions.
Results night: Ayame calls Media 'a consolation prize' within a PC's earshot; Sunny looks at that PC before answering.

fronts.name: Tatsuya's Restraint
fronts.goal: never hurt anyone, even if it costs the bout

moves.text: He wraps his hands in the training bays and won't spar at full strength.
In his own bout he blocks a teammate's hit and refuses to release it; his team loses (heard or seen between bouts).
He skips the post-results dinner unless someone goes after him.

antagonist.name: Daichi Sumeragi
antagonist.face: captain of the Final's opposing team (rebound clap); courteous, relentless, studies the 2B team's bouts
antagonist.first_contact: Day 6 morning in Chikara Battle Arena/training-bays: he bows to Tatsuya, then turns and studies the PCs.

clues.text: Sunny sits as far from the 1A rows as the gallery allows.
A 1A student whispers about 'that clip' when Sunny passes; her smile gets bigger, not smaller.
Sunny's phone lights up with a resurfaced comment thread and she flips it face down.
Asked about her old class, Sunny answers with a joke and a nickname, never a fact.

surprises: An opposing team's captain bows to Tatsuya
The medical team asks Yūto to cover the station
climax_options: The Final ends early on a cracked rule, and results night carries the weight
The Final goes the distance and the crowd remembers it
The Final is lost well, and the marks still honour how they fought
